notes:
**New**
- **Merged chat across sites**: when a streamer is live on Twitch, Kick and YouTube at once, see all their chats in one tab, without having their other streams on screen. Each message has a small mark showing where it came from. Refract suggests it when it finds the same streamer live elsewhere, or use the new merge button above any chat. Merges are remembered for next time.
- **Markers**: press **B** while watching (or ⋯ on a stream → Add marker) to mark a moment. Later, open the past broadcast right at that spot from Moments → Markers, and add notes to remember what happened.
- **While you were away**: after you've been gone a while, Overview shows who went live, who streamed and already ended, your mentions and raids, and what you earned.
- **Streamer mode**: hides your account name and picture, your sign-in details and what people wrote in mention pop-ups, so nothing private ends up on stream. It can turn on by itself while OBS, Streamlabs, XSplit or Twitch Studio is running, and can also hide who you follow. A red pill in the top bar shows when it's on.

**Fixed**
- **Smoother streams, less memory**:
  - Video now loads directly instead of being copied through the app first (Refract switches back by itself if your PC ever needs the old way).
  - Labels and buttons on top of the video no longer use a blur effect, which made the graphics card redo work on every frame.
  - **Ambient mode no longer causes lag.** It was the main cause of dropped frames (in testing it cut four streams to about 10 fps and dropped almost half the video frames). It's rebuilt from scratch: no blur and no live copy of the video, just soft color glows that are almost free to draw, with colors checked every few seconds. With it on, streams now play about as smoothly as with it off.
  - Chat only draws new messages instead of redrawing every line each time one arrives.
  - Streams keep a smaller buffer in memory.
- **Memory leaks fixed**: Refract no longer slowly uses more memory the longer it runs.
  - Closed streams were never fully freed (each closed tile, its video player included, stayed in memory).
  - Chat for channels you closed kept all its messages and every chatter's name forever. Now it's freed a few minutes after you close it.
  - Each channel you opened kept its own full copy of thousands of BTTV/FFZ/7TV emotes. Now only the 12 most recent are kept.
  - Ad-shield records piled up every time a stream reconnected.
  - Saved files (backups, Moments, Year in Refract) stayed in memory after saving.
  - In testing, opening and closing 160 streams with busy chats used to leave 30,000 page elements and ~21 MB stuck in memory; now it all goes back to where it started.
- **Streams stay close to live**: if a stream falls behind (after a stall or ad break), it quietly catches up instead of staying 20+ seconds behind.
- **Updating always gets the newest version**: if a newer version came out after the Update button appeared, you go straight to it instead of installing the one you missed first.
- The "What's new" window only shows the version you just updated to.
